items.title: Welcome & Overview
items.html:
🎉 Welcome to Countdown·DJS

Countdown·DJS puts your countdowns on the desktop, one floating window per project. Key capabilities:

  • Independent countdowns for every project: Each project owns its own floating window, with its own target date and an optional time precise to the minute.
  • Calendar days / workdays: Chinese public holidays and make-up workday rules are built in, so the remaining workdays are calculated and displayed automatically.
  • Recurring projects: Countdowns that repeat weekly, monthly or yearly — weekly meetings, the first-of-month exam, the annual company party. See [[ref:loop-settings]].
  • Layout Editor: Drag text, images, weather, the Pomodoro timer and other elements into place. See [[ref:layout-editor]].
  • Dynamic wallpaper engine: Five built-in animated backgrounds — Starfield, Mouse Particles, Aurora, Sky and Tide. Aurora and Sky prefer GPU rendering through OpenGL + GLSL. See [[ref:dynamic-wallpaper]].
  • Wallpaper Picker: Manage image collections and rotate them on an interval, either inside floating windows or as the system desktop wallpaper. See [[ref:wallpaper-picker]].
  • Standalone floating widgets: Place weather, Pomodoro and poem gadgets on the desktop on their own, with dragging, scaling and an independent theme. See [[ref:floating-widgets]].
  • Light and dark themes: Follow the system, or lock in light or dark. Every window and settings screen updates immediately. See [[ref:theme]].
  • Click-through mode: Clicks pass straight through a floating window to whatever sits beneath it. See [[ref:click-through]].
  • Backup and restore: Back up every project and setting to data/backups/ in one click, which makes migration and recovery easy.
  • Plugin system (CAC): Third-party plugins can add dynamic backgrounds, desktop widgets and settings panels. See "🔌 CAC Plugin System".

Topics are grouped by feature; select an entry on the left to read its description. When you hit a specific error or odd behaviour, start with "❓ FAQ", which lists troubleshooting steps by symptom.

items.title: Floating Window Operations
items.html:
🖱️ Basic Operations

  • Move the window: Hold the left mouse button anywhere inside the floating window (or press and hold with a finger in touch mode) and drag.
  • Resize: Move the pointer to an edge or corner of the window until it becomes a double-headed arrow, then drag. (In touch mode, dragging from an edge or corner can be a little awkward.)
  • Context menu: Right-click the floating window (in touch mode, press and hold for 3 seconds until a square appears, then release) to open a menu with Settings, Pin/Unpin Window, Fullscreen, Click-Through, Window Lock, Close Window and Quit.
  • Double-click action: Double-click anywhere in the floating window (touch mode may not support this) to open the Global Settings panel.
  • Fullscreen mode: Other windows are hidden automatically. Move the pointer to the bottom-right corner to reveal a floating control panel for opacity, dynamic wallpaper switching, frame rate and quality.

items.title: First-Time Setup
items.html:
⚙️ First-Time Setup Guide

  1. Create your first project: Right-click the floating window → Settings → Projects → Add Project. The default name is "新项目" and the target date is 30 days from today.
  2. Edit the project details: Select the project and click "Edit Project". You can change the name and the target date (format YYYY-MM-DD); enable "Set Exact Time" to specify hours and minutes.
  3. Adjust the appearance: With the project selected, click "Skins" to pick a preset or create a new skin. In the editor, drag elements into position and adjust colour, font, shadow and so on in the property panel on the right; every change applies immediately.
  4. Global Settings: On the "Global Settings" tab, choose the theme mode (Follow System / Light / Dark), interface language, render backend, auto start and GPU shader acceleration, then configure the weather source and city, log level and so on below.
  5. Plugins: Open the "Plugins" tab, switch the plugin system on first (it is off by default), then drop plugin .py files into the plugins folder, refresh (or restart) and enable them. Turning off the "启用插件系统" switch stops every running plugin at once and hides its widgets; turning it back on restores the plugins that were enabled before.

items.title: Creating a Project
items.html:
➕ Create a Project

In the settings panel → Projects → click "Add Project". Each project maps to its own floating window, and every parameter can be changed later in the Edit Project dialog.

items.title: Editing a Project
items.html:
✏️ Edit a Project

Select a project and click "Edit Project". The dialog contains the following settings:

  • Project name: Displayed in the title area of the floating window.
  • Target date: Format YYYY-MM-DD; you can also pick a date with the calendar button.
  • Exact time: When enabled, the countdown is precise to the hour and minute (HH:MM).
  • Show elapsed and remaining days together: Available for normal projects.
  • End sound: Enable one of eight built-in effects — "风铃", "钢琴", "叮叮", "哔哔", "长音", "闹钟渐响", "海浪潮汐" and "电子合成" — or point to a custom audio file.
  • Project type: Normal / Recurring, plus custom types registered by plugins.
  • Recurring settings: Weekly (pick the weekdays), monthly (pick the day of the month) or yearly (pick the month and day), with an optional end date.

Appearance settings — font, font size, colour, window opacity, background type, layout and so on — belong to "Skins" and the "Layout Editor", not to this dialog.

items.title: Recurring Project Settings
items.html:
🔄 Recurring Project Settings (Experimental)

Besides "Normal", a project can be switched to the "Recurring" type for countdowns that repeat on a cycle — weekly meetings, monthly exams, annual parties and the like.

Setup Steps

  1. In the "Edit Project" dialog, set Project Type to "Recurring" (or choose a recurring project when creating one).
  2. Expand the "Recurring Settings" area below:
    • Cycle type: Weekly / Monthly / Yearly.
    • Weekly: Tick the weekday(s) on which it triggers (Monday to Sunday; select at least one).
    • Monthly: Choose the day of the month (1–31). If the month has no such day, the last day of that month is used automatically — handy for first-of-month meetings, monthly exams and so on.
    • Yearly: Choose the month and day. If that date does not exist in the year, the last day of the month is used.
    • Target time: Reuses the "Target Time" (HH:MM) above as the trigger time on the day.
    • End date: Optional. Leave it empty for an endless cycle; once a date (format YYYY-MM-DD) is set, nothing triggers after it.
  3. After saving, the countdown works out the next matching trigger time and shows the time remaining.

Trigger Logic

  • Search forward from the current moment and jump to the first moment that matches the cycle and has not yet passed.
  • Once the trigger time arrives, the window rolls on to the next matching date automatically; no manual reset is needed.
  • If an end date was set and has passed, the floating window shows "已结束".

Tip: Recurring projects support skins, backgrounds, poems and every other element exactly like normal projects.

items.title: Skin Basics
items.html:
🎨 Skin Editor

Open it from the "Skins" button below the project list; select a project first, then click the button. The element list is on the left and lets you add or remove elements. In the preview area in the middle you can drag elements directly, with snapping and guide lines. The property panel on the right adjusts colour, font, outline and shadow for the selected element. Preview changes appear on the canvas immediately.

A skin can be designed twice — once for light and once for dark. Use the light/dark buttons at the top right of the editor to switch which set you are editing, and the adjacent "Sync to Light / Sync to Dark" button to copy the current set over the other one. On save, the set matching the project's light/dark policy is used automatically. If only one set has been designed, saving prompts "This skin will not support light/dark switching"; choosing "Yes" saves anyway, and the missing set keeps using the appearance that was designed.

These "skin light/dark sets" affect only the contents of the floating window and are separate from the interface theme: the interface theme changes the program screens such as the settings center and dialogs, while a skin changes the countdown window itself.

Custom skins can be edited in place: select one in the skin library and click "Edit" at the bottom right. The editor loads that skin's current light/dark appearance, and saving overwrites the original skin instead of creating a new one. If the current project uses a different skin, it is loaded temporarily for preview and restored when you cancel. Built-in skins cannot be edited; save them as a new skin instead.

The right property panel uses a single row of horizontal tabs: Font, Colour, Background, General, Effects and Layout. Clicking a tab switches the page, and only one page is shown at a time instead of stacked collapsible groups. Element-specific settings live in their matching tab: text content under Font, countdown settings, verses, tips, Pomodoro and weather under General, and shapes under Layout. With no element selected only the Background tab remains, so the window background stays directly adjustable.

The action bar at the bottom of the skin library lets you edit or delete skins you created. The built-in Classic skin has no delete entry. Before a custom skin is deleted, the projects currently using it are listed and deletion is confirmed twice; those projects then fall back to the default skin.

Each skin stores its own countdown display format — decimal days, days/hours/minutes, hours/minutes/seconds or a custom template — together with the skin. Editing or saving one skin does not affect another, and switching back to a skin restores the timing display it was saved with. The Classic skin always uses decimal-days timing.

items.title: Deleting a Project
items.html:
🗑️ Delete a Project

Select a project and click "Delete Project". After you confirm, the project is removed from the list, the floating window is rebuilt immediately and the change is written back to the configuration. Files already generated for the project are not deleted with it — to clean those up, remove them yourself under data/user. The last remaining project cannot be deleted; at least one must stay.

items.title: Light and Dark Themes
items.html:
Light and Dark Themes

In Settings Center → Global Settings, inside the "Global Settings" group and just below the "Language / Render Backend" row, you will find the "深浅色主题" dropdown. It offers three choices: Follow System (default), Light and Dark. The change takes effect at once — no restart — and the configuration file records it as theme_mode, so the last selection is reused after a restart.

Follow System reads the Windows "应用模式" preference (registry key AppsUseLightTheme). The app checks it every 2 seconds, so a system-level switch is picked up within 2 seconds. Choosing Light or Dark locks the mode in place; system changes are ignored.

Switching triggers the following: the settings window closes and reopens by itself, staying on the same page (if you were on page 4, you stay on page 4); every other open dialog, popup menu, tray menu, scrollbar, text box, button, progress bar and tooltip is recoloured too. Auxiliary windows such as the skin editor, if open, stay alive detached from their parent instead of being closed along with it.

Two areas deliberately do not change. First, project skins on floating windows: they are custom project appearance, so edit them in the skin editor. Second, the phase colours of standalone floating widgets (weather / Pomodoro / poem) — the three colours for focus, short break and long break — do not follow the interface theme by default, although the card background and text do change; the Pomodoro palette follows the accent colour only when "Follow Theme" is selected. Each widget's own colour scheme is chosen separately from its context menu item "配色模式", which offers Follow System / Auto (Sunset) / Dark / Light and does not interfere with the global setting described here.

Known behaviour: the settings window flashes briefly when it reopens, and its position and size are restored from the geometry saved last time. In fullscreen editing mode the floating toolbar stays dark and translucent because it sits on top of the wallpaper; it does not follow the interface theme.

items.title: Background Types
items.html:
🖼️ Background Types

  • Solid colour: A single-colour background with adjustable opacity. When opacity is < 1.0 and the corner radius is 0, Windows acrylic blur is enabled automatically (Windows 10/11 only).
  • Image: JPG, PNG, BMP and GIF are supported; GIFs animate. The image is stretched to fill the whole window and can be uploaded into the data/user directory while editing the project.
  • Gradient: A linear gradient with custom start and end colours, running from the upper left to the lower right.
  • Dynamic: Five built-in dynamic wallpapers — Starfield, Mouse Particles, Aurora, Sky and Tide. Frame rate (30/60/120 FPS) and quality (High/Medium/Low) are adjustable, and each background keeps its own display settings.
  • Transparent (experimental): no background
    • Aurora / Sky prefer GPU rendering with shaders (OpenGL Compatibility Profile + GLSL #version 330), 60 FPS by default. If the GPU is unavailable or acceleration is off, they fall back automatically to the CPU + numpy path (lower performance). Tide draws layered waves on the CPU with QPainter.
    • Sky in fullscreen mode draws a horizontal boarding-pass card in the lower-left corner with the project name, countdown and poem, keeping the design minimal so the background stays dominant.

items.title: Wallpaper Picker
items.html:
🖼️ Wallpaper Picker

The Wallpaper Picker is a standalone wallpaper module on the Settings Center → Wallpaper Selector tab. It manages a collection of images and rotates them on a configurable interval, and the result can be applied either as the floating window background or directly as the system desktop wallpaper.

Image Management

  • Add Image: Click "Add Image" and choose local pictures (JPG/PNG/BMP and so on); multiple selection is allowed.
  • Remove: Select an image in the list and click "Remove" to take it out (it is removed from the list only, not from disk).
  • Move Up / Move Down: Reorder the list, which determines playback order in "Sequential" mode.

Slideshow Settings

  • Enable Slideshow: Tick this to start switching wallpapers on the interval.
  • Switch Mode: Sequential (stops at the end) / Random / Loop (default, cycles through the list in order).
  • Interval (sec): In seconds, 60 by default.
  • Fill Mode: Stretch / Fit / Center / Tile.
  • Fade Transition: Tick this for a fade in and out when the wallpaper changes.

Targets

  • Apply to Floating Window: Shows the current wallpaper as the floating window background.
  • Apply to Desktop: Calls the system API to set the desktop wallpaper directly (supported on Windows, macOS and Linux).
  • Dual Screen: When ticked, separate wallpapers can be assigned to the main and secondary screens.

Tip: The Wallpaper Picker is independent of a project's "image background". If you want a floating window to follow the slideshow, choose the source provided by the Wallpaper Picker as the project's background type.

items.title: Text Element Styling
items.html:
📝 Text Element Styling

Select any text element on the right side of the layout editor (name, countdown, static text and so on). The right property panel uses a row of horizontal tabs; click a tab to switch, and only one page is shown at a time:

  • Font: Font size 6 to 72 pixels and font family
  • Colour: Text colour, opacity and follow background
  • Background: Background colour and radius for the selected element, plus window opacity, background type and window background colour/gradient/image/dynamic options
  • General: Visibility, automatic width, width/height, and element-specific settings such as the countdown
  • Effects: Outline and shadow
  • Layout: Alignment and position

The countdown display format lives in the General tab: choose decimal days, days/hours/minutes, hours/minutes/seconds or a custom template. Custom templates use {days}, {hours}, {minutes} and {seconds} placeholders; when a placeholder is not followed by a unit, the matching unit is appended automatically, so {seconds} alone renders as “18秒”. The 天 / 时 / 分 / 秒 buttons below the field insert placeholders with their units.

"Follow background" only appears on Verse Flow and tip elements. When enabled, the text inverts automatically against the background behind it: light backgrounds get dark text, dark backgrounds get light text. Picking a colour manually unties it from the background; leave it unchecked to keep a fixed colour. The switch is independent of skins and recalculates whenever the window background changes.

items.title: Layout Editor
items.html:
🌐 Layout Editor Tips

  • Drag to position: Press and drag elements directly on the preview canvas; positions are stored as percentages relative to the window width and height.
  • Grid and snapping: Turn on "网格" to show helper cells, and "吸附" to snap dragged elements to other elements or guide lines (thirds and centre lines).
  • Guides: Show the horizontal/vertical centre lines and the thirds lines to help with precise alignment.
  • Element order: Use "Move Up" and "Move Down" to change rendering order; newly added elements sit on top by default.
  • Add custom elements: Click the "添加" button to add custom text or a custom image. Text content is freely editable; an image can be picked from disk (it is copied into the user directory automatically).
  • Delete elements: Select an element and click "删除" (the project name and countdown cannot be deleted for now).

items.title: How Dynamic Wallpapers Work
items.html:
✨ How Dynamic Wallpapers Work

The app ships five built-in animated backgrounds, each designed for a different visual mood:

  • Starfield: Hundreds of stars with random brightness drift slowly to the left while their brightness flickers in cycles, imitating a night sky.
  • Mouse Particles: A large field of coloured dots with initial velocities. Moving the mouse exerts an "attraction" or "repulsion" on the particles, and pairs closer than a threshold are joined by lines; clicking the window sends out a ripple.
  • Aurora: A GLSL fragment shader inside QOpenGLWindow draws five volumetric light curtains (green / cyan / purple / pink / blue-green) in real time. Three layers of fbm organic noise drive the width and height of the curtains, a nebula texture is overlaid on top, and the result is a soft 3D aurora in perspective. It requires "实验性：GPU 着色器加速" to be enabled in Global Settings and OpenGL support on the system; otherwise it falls back automatically to the CPU + numpy version (same visual quality, higher CPU load).
  • Tide: The CPU and QPainter draw a deep blue sea surface with four sine waves; HSV gradient light bands ride on the wave crests to produce slow, rolling swells.
  • Sky (early morning): Golden-hour sky + 4 FBM clouds + sun glow + god rays. This one also prefers the GPU shader path (60 FPS by default) and needs "实验性：GPU 着色器加速" in Global Settings, with the same fallback as Aurora. With shaders, the quality setting adjusts the FBM octave count, cloud count and whether light beams are computed, and built-in frame-time monitoring performs automatic downgrade and recovery. In fullscreen mode a horizontal boarding-pass card in the lower-left corner shows the project information and countdown, kept minimal so the background stays dominant.

GPU Shader Engine

Aurora and Sky render with OpenGL 3.3 Compatibility Profile + GLSL #version 330. To work across different graphics drivers, the engine probes several function sets in turn and tries each context below, maximising compatibility:

  1. 3.3 Compatibility Profile (recommended)
  2. 4.1 Core Profile
  3. 2.0 NoProfile (final fallback)

Once a usable context is found, the matching OpenGL function pointers are resolved and the shader program is initialised.

Automatic Downgrade and CPU Fallback

  • Automatic shader downgrade: Built-in frame-time monitoring detects performance pressure and lowers quality (fewer FBM octaves, fewer clouds, skipping light-beam computation) or reduces the frame rate; it ramps back up when performance recovers.
  • CPU fallback: When the GPU is unavailable or acceleration is off, rendering uses numpy + QPainter with the same adaptive downgrade logic (quality and frame rate adjust to frame time).
  • Render pausing: GL rendering pauses automatically while a context menu, combo box or layout editor dialog is in use; hovering over a panel drops it to 12 FPS and moving away restores it.

Boarding-Pass Poem Display

In Sky fullscreen mode the boarding-pass card in the lower-left corner shows a poem: a random one switches in from the poem library every 10 seconds, displayed at the bottom of the right side of the divider (the tear line), so that the card reads as a flight information panel together with the project name and countdown. See [[ref:poem-carousel]].

You can adjust the frame rate and quality of a dynamic wallpaper from the control panel in fullscreen mode or in the project editor. In fullscreen mode, display settings and frame rate are saved per background: every background (Starfield, Particles, Aurora, Sky and so on) keeps its own frame rate and quality, and switching loads that background's saved settings without affecting the others.

items.title: Pomodoro Timer
items.html:
🍅 Using the Pomodoro Timer

The Pomodoro timer comes in two forms, and they are fully independent in layout and interaction:

Pomodoro inside a project (clock face)

Once you add a "Pomodoro" element in the layout editor, it is drawn as a clock face: a 1px rim, 60 hairline tick marks, a very fine hand outside the ring and a narrow angular numeral in the centre, with a cycle-beat segment along the top and phase dot labels along the bottom. The face scales proportionally with the element size.

  • Single click (a single finger tap in touch mode): Start or pause the current timer.
  • Double click (may not be supported in touch mode): Reset the current phase.
  • Context menu: Start/Pause, Reset Current Phase, Skip to Next Phase, Reset All.
  • In the editor you can set the focus length (25 minutes by default), short break (5 minutes by default), long break length and long-break interval, and choose the face colour scheme, whether progress ticks are shown, auto-start of the next phase and a phase-end chime.

Standalone floating Pomodoro (timeline)

Added to the desktop through "Add Widget", it is drawn as a timeline: a hairline track, quarter tick marks, the elapsed segment in the phase colour, a glowing cursor and duration labels at both ends, with a phase label at the top left and a cycle-beat segment at the top right.

  • Click to start or pause, double-click to reset the current phase, and use the context menu to skip to the next phase or reset everything.
  • When a phase ends, a chime from data/sounds/ plays (skipping to the next phase manually does not play it).
  • Phase colours: focus runs from coral to amber, short break is teal, long break is indigo.

items.title: Weather Widget Setup
items.html:
🌤️ Weather Widget Setup

Add a "Weather" element in the layout editor, then choose the province and city in the property panel on the right. The in-project weather widget uses a circular ring + icon + temperature + city design, and the ring colour changes with the weather (sunny = orange, cloudy = blue-grey, rain = blue, snow = white, thunder = purple, overcast = grey, fog = grey). The standalone weather widget uses a flat design instead: a vertical weather colour bar, city and description, a thin divider, a narrow angular temperature and a weather icon.

Data Source

Choose one under Global Settings → Weather Source:

  • QWeather (和风天气) (default): You must open your own account in the QWeather console and enter your API Key and Host (click "📖 如何开通和风天气 API" next to the weather source to open the sign-up guide). Until that is done, the widget reports "未配置和风天气 API Key". You can also enter your own API Key and Host under "Custom".
  • Custom: Enter a custom URL template (the {city} placeholder stands for the city name); a plain-text response is displayed on the widget as-is.

Widget Size

The weather widget does not use "auto width"; set its pixel size directly with the width/height sliders in the property panel (minimum 72×88). The preview matches the rendered size exactly.

Refresh Strategy

  • Data is fetched automatically 3 seconds after the window starts, refreshed when window visibility changes, and then refreshed every 30 minutes.
  • Clicking the weather widget opens a 7-day forecast window (hourly temperature, precipitation probability, AQI and dressing index), which requires a successful latitude/longitude lookup first.

Troubleshooting

  • If "获取天气..." or "天气离线" stays on screen for a long time, check the network connection and the API Key, or try restarting the app.
  • If a city name appears in pinyin, the QWeather GeoAPI returns pinyin for some cities; the app already falls back to the Chinese name of the parent administrative region, so no action is needed.

items.title: Poem and Quote Carousel
items.html:
📜 Poem and Quote Carousel

The poem level now lives in the properties of the "Skin Editor → Verse Flow" element, so the source can be set per project:

  • None: No poem; a short tip such as "保持专注" is shown instead.
  • Primary: Simple, easy short lines and verses.
  • Junior: Well-known classical lines.
  • Senior: Longer or more profound verses.
  • Extra: A collection of classic lines from outside the syllabus.

Every so often (15 minutes by default, changeable in the project editor) a poem types itself onto the floating window, character by character. The poem data lives in data/poems.json, split into the four levels primary / junior / senior / extra, and you can add or remove entries yourself. Verse Flow text colour is under "Colour" on the right: enabling "Follow background" inverts it against the background automatically (dark text on light, light text on dark), and it is on by default. Picking a colour manually turns it off and fixes the colour you chose.

Boarding-Pass Poems

In Sky fullscreen mode, the boarding-pass card in the lower-left corner shows poems automatically: a random one switches in from the poem library every 10 seconds, displayed at the bottom of the right side of the divider (the tear line). When the library is empty or not loaded, the card shows the default line "保持专注 · 享受当下". Boarding-pass poems and the "Verse Flow" element on the floating window work independently and can be shown at the same time.

items.title: Standalone Floating Widgets
items.html:
Standalone Floating Widgets

These are desktop gadgets that are not attached to any countdown project. Add and remove them under Settings Center → Projects → Add Widget. There are three kinds:

  • Weather: A vertical colour bar, city and weather description, a divider, narrow temperature and a weather icon. Data refreshes every 30 minutes, and a message is shown on the widget when it fails.
  • Pomodoro: A phase label (filled while running, outlined while paused, grey while idle) + a cycle block + remaining time + a progress bar (quarter ticks and a cursor) + duration axes at both ends.
  • Poem: Vertical text, one column per line, with the first line on the far right and subsequent lines moving left; the source occupies its own column on the far left, rendered in a regular script typeface.

Press inside the widget to drag it, and the position is written when you release. The mouse wheel scales it in 5% steps, up to 760 pixels on one side. Each of the four edges and four corners has a 9-pixel hotspot; dragging there resizes the widget, and the cursor changes to match the direction. All of these sizes and positions are stored in the configuration and restored after a restart.

Context menu: Pin, Click-Through, "配色模式" (Follow System / Auto (Sunset) / Dark / Light, Follow System by default), Enlarge, Shrink, Remove Widget. Auto (Sunset) switches between light and dark at sunset according to the weather service; when no sunset data is available it falls back to a fixed window — 20:00 to 08:00 counts as dark.

For the Pomodoro widget, click to start or pause, double-click to reset the current phase, and use the context menu to skip to the next phase or reset everything. A phase ending plays a chime from data/sounds/; skipping manually stays silent.

Once click-through is on, the widget stops responding to the mouse and even its context menu cannot be opened. The app provides no reverse switch, so the only way back is to remove the widget in the Add Widget dialog and add it again.

items.title: Custom Text and Images
items.html:
➕ Add Custom Text or Image

In the layout editor, click the "添加" button and choose "自定义文字" or "自定义图片".

  • 自定义文字: Enter any text; afterwards it can be moved, coloured and styled just like other text elements.
  • 自定义图片: Choose a local image file (PNG/JPG/GIF and so on). The image is copied into data/user/ and shown on the floating window. Its size can also be adjusted in the property panel.

items.title: Click-Through Mode
items.html:
🖱️ Click-Through Mode

Click-through makes a floating window stop receiving mouse events, so every click passes straight to the window or desktop underneath while the countdown keeps rendering normally. It suits setups where the countdown is purely a display layer and must never get in the way.

How to Enable

  • Context menu: Right-click the floating window → tick "🖱️ Click-Through". This item is a toggle; click it again to turn it off.
  • Once enabled, the floating window can no longer be dragged with the left button or right-clicked. Open the settings from the system tray menu, or cancel click-through from the tray, to get control back.

Notes

  • The click-through state is saved with the project and persists across restarts.
  • While click-through is on, the floating window's context menu cannot open either; use the tray icon instead.
  • Combining window pinning with click-through gives a desktop decoration that stays visible without blocking anything.
  • While click-through is on, the window smoothly fades within 180 ms when the pointer comes within roughly 38 px of its edge, down to about half of your configured opacity and never below 32%. It returns to your configured opacity once the pointer moves about 78 px away. The enter and leave distances differ so the window does not flicker when the pointer sits on the boundary. The fade is a temporary display effect and never rewrites the saved opacity.

items.title: Window Lock
items.html:
🔒 Window Lock

With window lock on, a floating window cannot be dragged or resized with the left mouse button, but it still receives the mouse and fires mouse events (click interactions, context menu, hover) and keeps displaying its content. It suits situations where the layout is final and you do not want accidental drags.

How to Enable

  • Context menu: Right-click the floating window → tick "Window Lock". This item is a toggle; click it again to turn it off.
  • Settings can still be opened while locked; turn the lock off first if you need to move the window.

Notes

  • The lock state is saved with the project and persists across restarts.
  • Unlike click-through: click-through receives no mouse events at all, whereas lock only blocks dragging and resizing while mouse interaction still works.

items.title: Installing Plugins
items.html:
📥 How to Install Third-Party Plugins

  1. Get the plugin file: A plugin is a single .py file, usually provided by the community or its developer.
  2. Place the plugin: Copy the .py file into the plugins folder in the application directory (create the folder yourself if it does not exist).
  3. Enable the plugin system: Open Settings → Plugins and make sure the "启用插件系统" switch at the top is on.
  4. Refresh the list: The plugin loads automatically and appears in the list.
  5. Enable the plugin: Select it and click "Enable". If it declares baseline permissions, a permission modal explains each item's purpose and risk and lets you choose the grant scope; rejecting a baseline permission cancels this enable action. Advanced permissions are not shown here — the plugin requests them on demand when it actually needs them.

Note: the plugin system is globally disabled by default for security. Install plugins only from sources you trust.

items.title: Managing Plugins and Permissions
items.html:
⚙️ Managing Plugins

On the Plugins tab, each plugin shows its name, version, author, status, required permissions and risk level.

  • Enable/Disable: Controls whether the plugin runs. A disabled plugin executes no code. Enabling shows a modal once for baseline permissions only; advanced permissions are requested on demand when the plugin actually uses them.
  • Permissions: Clicking "授权级别…" lists all 20 permission bits, each of which can be set to Not granted / Allow once / This session / Always allow / Deny and remember. Bits that are wired up but were never declared by the plugin show Not declared, which differs from Not granted; a manual grant takes effect immediately and is synced to the plugin host process.
  • Restore all legacy permissions: Only for plugins that use a legacy declaration. The old declaration is split into "baseline permissions + on-demand permissions"; if that breaks a feature, click this to restore everything the legacy declaration covered in one go. The action requires a CAPTCHA and is written to the sensitive operation audit.
  • Plugin details: Selecting a plugin shows its details on the right, including the plugin's own settings panel if it provides one. If the plugin is blocked by permissions during registration, the status column reads "Start failed" and the details give the reason, so you never end up with a plugin that looks enabled but has no working features.
  • Logs: The "常规日志" area below shows the plugin's runtime log, while "Sensitive Operations" records every file, network and command call the plugin makes.

items.title: Permission Model
items.html:
🔒 Plugin Permission Model

Plugin permissions come in two tiers: baseline permissions and advanced permissions. What the manifest and code declare is the "requested" value, not the "granted" value; permissions reach the grant table only after you confirm them in a dialog or set them manually in the permission manager.

Two Tiers

  • Baseline permissions: Capabilities a plugin needs on enable or on first display, confirmed once in a single modal when it starts. Low- and medium-risk bits (file read/write, network access, sockets, clipboard, system information, notifications, UI injection, event listening, background threads) all belong here; only high-risk bits become on-demand. If baseline permissions exceed 12 items, they are truncated from highest risk down, and the plugin details list exactly which permissions were cut and why.
  • Advanced permissions: Deleting files, running commands, starting processes, the registry, environment variables, dynamic execution, autostart, reading other plugins' source and so on. They are absent at enable time and are requested only when the plugin actually needs the feature; high-risk on-demand requests escalate to a modal, while the rest use a lightweight card in the lower-right corner.
  • Manifest v2: In plugin.json a plugin can declare baseline (an array of baseline permission names) and on_demand (each entry with perm, feature, title, reason and fallback) through permissions_v2. Legacy manifests that only carry an integer permissions are migrated automatically: low- and medium-risk bits become baseline, high-risk bits become on-demand, and default reasons are generated.
  • Reason field: Every on-demand permission has a "request reason" taken from the plugin manifest; when the plugin gives none, it shows "The plugin did not explain what this is used for.", followed by a note that the host supplied this explanation, so the field is never blank.

Four Grant Levels and Anti-Nagging

  • Allow once: Expires immediately after one operation; a failed attempt still consumes the single try.
  • This session: Valid for the lifetime of the process and reverts to Not granted after a restart.
  • Always allow: Persists across restarts and can be revoked in the permission manager at any time.
  • Deny and remember: Keeps blocking that permission with no further prompts; it can only be revoked manually in the Security Center.
  • 5-minute cooldown: For five minutes after you cancel, close or time out a prompt, the same plugin and permission produce no new prompt — the request is quietly blocked and logged. The cooldown is cleared on restart, so the plugin may ask once again.
  • Rate limit: A single plugin gets at most 4 prompts in 60 seconds; beyond that, requests are quietly blocked for the rest of the session and logged.

Two Request Paths

  • Explicit request (primary path): The plugin calls api.request_permission(permission, feature, reason) when the user clicks an advanced feature. An existing grant returns True immediately; denial, cooldown or an undeclared permission returns False with no prompt. The plugin should mark the feature as "needs permission" rather than retrying endlessly.
  • Ask after interception (fallback): Available only for network access and the clipboard, and the plugin must explicitly declare fallback: true in its manifest. Commands, processes, the registry, dynamic execution, file deletion, autostart and plugin-source reads are hard-blocked and never prompt.
  • Side effect of the fallback: The fallback path is "fail first, remedy later". Once you allow it, the intercepted operation continues automatically — no exception, no retry needed, and the security event is recorded as granted_retry. To avoid these prompts entirely, turn off "拦截后弹出权限询问" in the Security Center; the fallback then hard-blocks and logs.
  • Graceful failure: After an explicit request is denied, the plugin should show an inline "needs permission / skipped this time" state rather than a stack trace or a system error dialog, and leave other features unaffected.

Four-Layer Attribution (same vocabulary for UI and plugins)

  • L1 Declaration: whether the manifest declares the capability. When it does not, the UI shows "Not declared", and only editing the manifest unlocks it.
  • L2 Grant: the level you gave. Not granted, deny-and-remember, cooldown, rate limit, prompt in progress, timeout and cancel all live here.
  • L3 Scope: the permission was granted, but the target sits in a protected zone (app configuration, other plugins' source, system directories, startup folders). Point the operation elsewhere or add the matching permission.
  • L4 Enforcement: hard rules that protect the host and the security machinery itself (dangerous modules, tampering with security hooks, reflection escaping through dunder access, sealed widget classes (observation only for now), disabled plugins, unattributable plugins). Never unlocked.

One-sentence mental model: a plugin must first be allowed by what it declared (L1), then have your grant (L2), then land on an allowed location (L3); L4 never opens. The Security Center and the interception card both name the layer, so when "the permission is there but it still fails", look at L3 first.

Structured Denials and Plugin Fallbacks

  • Exception fields: the raised PluginPermissionDenied is still a PermissionError subclass and its message is unchanged, but it now carries code, permission, permission_bit, capability, scope, denied_by, layer, retryable, unlockable, unlock_action, retry_after_ms, origin and target, plus exc.to_dict(). Branch on code, never on the message text.
  • Preflight: api.can(permission, target, event) decides without executing; api.explain reports the layer and the unlock entry; api.capabilities() returns declarations, levels, denial records, protected zones, hard rules and trusted state in one snapshot.
  • Fallbacks: api.permission_state reports one permission; api.on_denial(callback) receives the same structure for denials from any source; api.call_with_fallback(permission, primary, fallback) turns fail-fast into fail-with-fallback; api.declare_degraded records the promise in the Security Center.
  • Blocked imports: dangerous module imports raise PluginHardBlockDenied, which subclasses ImportError, so existing except ImportError handlers keep working.
  • Request results: request_permission returns a bool-compatible PermissionResult; if api.request_permission(...) is unchanged, while .code, .denial, .retryable and .unlockable distinguish all seven outcomes.

Observation Mode

The reflection dunder guard, cross-plugin service and data sharing, the api._app facade and runtime widget-class rewrites are in observation mode: the new rules only record, never block, and security events are tagged observe with what would have been blocked. Once existing plugins are confirmed unaffected, they will be tightened.

PluginPermission defines 24 permission bits (an IntFlag bit mask):

PermissionDescription
FILE_READReads files in the user and data directories. Excludes other plugins' source (requires PLUGIN_SOURCE) and system directories (requires SYSTEM_INFO)
FILE_WRITECreates, overwrites and appends files in the user and data directories. Cannot write to the startup folder (requires AUTOSTART), to protected configuration or to plugin source
FILE_DELETEDeletes and renames files and removes directories. Excludes deletions inside the startup folder (requires AUTOSTART)
NETWORKMaster switch for network access. Once granted, it covers socket creation, HTTP requests and direct sockets
NETWORK_HTTPSends HTTP requests (urllib / http.client). Excludes port listening and raw packet sending
NETWORK_SOCKETListens on ports, binds addresses and sends raw packets. Excludes high-level HTTP
COMMANDMaster switch for running system commands (such as os.system)
COMMAND_EXECChild process execution (spawn / subprocess calls)
CLIPBOARDReads and writes text, images and MIME data through the clipboard
SYSTEM_INFOReads system information. This bit alone grants access to system directories (such as C:\Windows), Program Files and ProgramData without FILE_READ; user directories outside that scope are unaffected by it
NOTIFICATIONSends system notifications through the host API
UI_INJECTRegisters floating widgets, settings panels, card slots and toolbar buttons, and injects methods into widget classes
EVENT_LISTENSubscribes to application events through api.hook
THREAD_SPAWNCreates threads
PROCESS_SPAWNCreates child processes
REGISTRYReads and writes the registry (Windows). Importing the registry module is still blocked outright for now
ENV_READReads and writes environment variables (reading and writing share this bit)
DANGEROUS_EVALDynamic execution through eval / exec / compile (extremely high risk)
AUTOSTARTAutostart at boot. This bit alone is enough and FILE_WRITE is not required: it can write directly into the current-user and common Startup folders, and it can call api.set_autostart(name, path, enable) so the host writes the Run key under HKCU. A plugin cannot import winreg itself and has no direct registry access; Run / RunOnce can only be written through the host API. Conversely, FILE_WRITE cannot write to those locations. Creating, renaming, deleting and changing permissions inside the Startup folder also fall under this bit
PLUGIN_SOURCEReads other plugins' source. This bit alone is enough and FILE_READ is not required; FILE_READ does not cover other plugins' source. A plugin's own modules can be exempted with own_modules in its manifest; without that declaration, files sharing the main file name prefix are allowed as a fallback, and the log states that the fallback was used. Reading its own modules still requires FILE_READ
UI_READReads host UI structure: window list, theme values and registered slots. Read-only, no rewriting
UI_MUTATERewrites class attributes and class methods on host or plugin widget classes, and replaces widget classes at runtime; changing a single instance needs no permission. Runtime rewrites are currently only recorded as seal.widget_class observations; api.bind_behavior requires it
PLUGIN_CALLCalls services published by other plugins. Both provider and caller must declare it, and trusted mode does not relax it
PLUGIN_DATA_SHAREReserved for cross-plugin data sharing. This version has no exports.data file-sharing interface; use public services for cross-plugin communication

Not declared vs. Not granted: When a permission bit is wired up but the plugin manifest never requested it, the grant window shows Not declared; when the plugin declared it but it was not granted, the window shows Not granted. Not declared does not mean the host lacks support — you can still set a level manually, and it takes effect immediately.

Legacy migration and restore: Plugins whose legacy manifest only has an integer permissions value are split automatically by risk: every low- and medium-risk bit becomes baseline, and only high-risk bits become on-demand. Migration only affects "whether a new confirmation is needed"; it never silently grants high-risk capabilities. If a feature stops working after migration, click "Restore all legacy permissions" in the Plugin Security Center; it requires a CAPTCHA, restores every permission the legacy declaration covered (high-risk included) as Always allow in one go, and writes the result to the sensitive operation audit.

At runtime the Python audit hook intercepts sensitive operations. If a plugin lacks the matching permission, a PermissionError is raised, the operation is blocked and the event is logged. Permission decisions do not depend on the "详细记录放行的敏感操作" switch: turning that switch off only reduces allowed records, it never weakens interception. If a sensitive operation comes from plugin code but the specific plugin cannot be identified, the hook rejects it as coming from an "unknown plugin" rather than letting it through.

items.title: Trust Mode (L4)
items.html:
🔐 Trust Mode (L4)

Trust mode lowers how aggressively the Security Center interferes with a single plugin. It suits plugins whose source you have reviewed, whose origin you trust and that you intend to keep. It is not a global switch: every plugin has its own persistent trust flag that survives restarts.

Scope and Enabling

  • Per plugin: Select a plugin on the "Plugin Security Center → Trust Mode" tab and switch it on; only that plugin is affected.
  • Requires a CAPTCHA: Enabling shares the same "type the characters you see" challenge as disabling the Security Center. A risk notice appears first, and the CAPTCHA follows once you confirm; a wrong code can be retried up to 3 times, and you can cancel at any point.
  • Revocable at any time: Revoking needs no CAPTCHA and takes effect immediately — the plugin is audited and permission-checked again right away.

What Is Relaxed Once Enabled

  • Sensitive-operation auditing is off for that plugin: Allowed file and network operations no longer produce allowed records, but blocked operations are still recorded.
  • Command permission becomes soft: Commands and process creation still require the plugin to actually hold the corresponding permission; without it they remain hard-blocked. Trust never hands out command capability automatically.
  • Path allowlist is widened: Apart from the program's protected files, any path can be read or written without per-call file read/write interception.
  • Configuration reads are opened up: Ordinary configuration files under data can be read.

What Is Still Blocked

  • Unauthorised system-level commands and process creation (os.system, os.exec, spawn, subprocess and the like).
  • Writing the program's own files (countdown_config.json, plugin_security.json, plugin_settings.json) or plugin source files.
  • Importing dangerous modules (ctypes, subprocess, winreg, importlib, pickle and so on).
  • Tampering with the audit hook (sys.addaudithook, sys.settrace, sys.setprofile).

Relation to Permissions

Trust does not mean a grant. The trust flag and the grant table are independent: enabling trust never writes the plugin's requested permissions into the grant table — permissions still follow the boxes you ticked in the permission manager — and revoking trust does not change any already granted permission bit.

Auditing and Persistence

Both enabling and revoking are written to the sensitive operation audit, recording the plugin name, time and action. Trust status is stored under trusted_plugins in data/plugin_security.json and stays in force across restarts; the entry is removed as soon as trust is revoked.

Risk

Trust mode noticeably reduces the visibility and interception strength for that plugin, so enable it only for plugins whose source you have reviewed and whose origin you trust. After a plugin update, revoke trust first, confirm how the new version behaves, then enable it again.

items.title: Plugin Development: Quick Start
items.html:
🛠️ Writing Your Own Plugin?

A plugin is a standard Python file. It must contain a setup(app, api) function and return an instance of a class that inherits from Plugin.

Plugins run in a separate child process, so a crash or an infinite loop cannot affect the main program. The only channel between a plugin and the main program is the plugin API:

  • app is a read-only proxy exposing only a few attributes such as app.data_dir and app.theme. Do not touch main-program windows or internal objects.
  • Widget classes returned by a plugin are instantiated in the child process; the host displays them as top-level frameless windows and then embeds them in the interface. Widgets must paint their own background.
  • Event callback arguments (on_window_create and so on) are JSON-serialised, so they cannot carry QWidget / QObject instances — stick to primitive types, dictionaries or objects with to_dict().
  • Introspection entry points such as sys.modules, __subclasses__ and __globals__ are forbidden; a plugin containing such code is rejected at load time.
# my_first_plugin.py
from djs_pyqt6 import Plugin, PluginPermission

class HelloWorldPlugin(Plugin):
    def __init__(self, app, api):
        super().__init__()
        self.name = "Hello World"
        self.version = "1.0"
        self.author = "YourName"
        self.description = "示例"
        # 声明需要的权限（本例不需要任何权限）
        self.requested_permissions = PluginPermission.NONE

    def on_enable(self):
        self.api.log("插件已启用")
        self.api.show_notification("Hello", "插件开始运行！")

def setup(app, api):
    return HelloWorldPlugin(app, api)

Save the code above as a .py file, put it in the plugins folder and enable the plugin in the app to see the notification.

Registering a Custom Dynamic Background

A plugin can register a custom dynamic background through api.register_dynamic_bg(id_name, display_name, widget_class, border_radius=None). The background class must inherit from QWidget and implement the following interface so the app can schedule it uniformly:

  • set_fps(fps): Sets the target frame rate (30/60/120).
  • set_quality(quality): Sets the quality ("high"/"medium"/"low").
  • set_radius(radius): Sets the corner radius (kept in sync with the floating window's corners).
class MyBgWidget(QWidget):
    def set_fps(self, fps): ...
    def set_quality(self, q): ...
    def set_radius(self, r): ...

class MyPlugin(Plugin):
    def on_enable(self):
        self.api.register_dynamic_bg("my_bg", "我的背景", MyBgWidget, border_radius=12)

Registering a GPU Shader Background

To register a GPU shader background, check HAS_OPENGL first (a global exported by the app's top level) and then render with QOpenGLWindow. GLSL #version 330 is recommended for shader code to keep compatibility:

try:
    from PyQt6.QtOpenGL import QOpenGLWindow
    import djs_pyqt6 as app_mod
    HAS_OPENGL = app_mod.HAS_OPENGL
except Exception:
    HAS_OPENGL = False

if HAS_OPENGL:
    class MyShaderWindow(QOpenGLWindow):
        _FS_SRC = '''#version 330
        varying vec2 vUv;
        uniform float uTime;
        void main() { gl_FragColor = vec4(vUv, 0.5+0.5*sin(uTime), 1.0); }'''
        # ... initializeGL / paintGL / resizeGL ...

Registration works exactly like an ordinary background: api.register_dynamic_bg("my_shader_bg", "我的着色器背景", MyShaderWindow).

Registering Desktop Widgets and Settings Panels

  • api.register_widget(id_name, display_name, widget_class): Registers a custom desktop widget.
  • api.register_settings_panel(id_name, display_name, widget_class) or api.register_settings_widget(...): Registers a plugin settings panel, shown in the plugin details area of the Plugins tab.

items.title: Plugin API Reference
items.html:
📘 PluginAPI Method Reference

Inside plugin code, the following methods are available through self.api:

MethodDescription
api.log(message, level="INFO")Writes a log entry, shown under "常规日志" in the Plugins tab.
api.register_dynamic_bg(id_name, display_name, widget_class, border_radius=None)Registers a custom dynamic background. The class must inherit from QWidget and should implement set_fps / set_quality / set_radius. GPU shader backgrounds are allowed (check HAS_OPENGL and use QOpenGLWindow).
api.update_dynamic_bg_radius(id_name, border_radius)Updates the corner radius of a registered background dynamically; it applies at once to every floating window using that background.
api.register_settings_panel(id_name, display_name, widget_class)Registers a plugin settings panel, shown in the plugin details area.
api.register_widget(id_name, display_name, widget_class)Registers a custom desktop widget.
api.register_float_widget(id_name, display_name, widget_class, default_size=(200, 200), description="", gpu=False)Registers a floating widget that can be placed on the desktop independently; it appears in the "独立控件" list of the context menu.
api.register_fullscreen_skin(id_name, display_name, widget_class, description="", gpu=False)Registers a fullscreen skin. It appears only in the fullscreen background selector and is no longer duplicated into dynamic backgrounds or the project window background dropdown.
api.register_settings_widget(id_name, display_name, widget_class)Equivalent to register_settings_panel.
api.get_config(key, default=None)Reads the plugin configuration (stored as JSON).
api.set_config(key, value)Saves the plugin configuration.
api.show_notification(title, message)Shows a system notification (requires system tray icon support).
api.request_permission(permission, feature="", reason="", timeout_ms=60000)Explicitly requests a single permission when the user clicks an advanced feature, returning a bool. The permission may be given as PluginPermission.NETWORK, an integer or the string "NETWORK". A prompt is possible only after it is declared in permissions_v2.on_demand; an undeclared permission, a "Deny and remember" hit, the 5-minute cooldown or the rate limit all return False without a prompt, and the plugin should disable that feature gracefully. An existing grant returns True immediately.
api.request_permissions(permissions, feature="", reason="", timeout_ms=60000)Use this when one feature genuinely needs 2–3 permissions; they are granted one by one, True is returned only if all succeed, and more than 3 items returns False straight away. There is no "grant all permanently" bundle.
api.permission_status(permission)Returns "permanent" / "session" / "once" / "none" / "deny" / "unknown", which lets the plugin grey out advanced buttons at startup instead of prompting and then failing.
api.set_autostart(name, path, enable=True)Has the host process write the Run key under HKCU (requires AUTOSTART). name may contain only letters, digits, spaces, dots, underscores and hyphens, up to 64 characters; path must be an existing absolute path; enable=False removes the entry with that name. A plugin cannot import winreg itself and cannot read or write the registry directly.
api.hook(name, callback, priority=100)Registers an event hook; lower numbers run first. The callback receives a context dict and may return {"action": "allow"}, {"action": "modify", "value": {...}} or {"action": "deny", "reason": "..."}.
api.register_action(scope, action_id, label, callback, icon="")Registers an action for window_menu (the window context menu), tray_menu (the tray menu) or settings_toolbar (the toolbar of the Plugins tab). The callback receives the current project context.
api.provide_service(name, handler)Exposes a service to other plugins; each name belongs to one plugin.
api.call_service(name, *args, **kwargs)Calls a service provided by another plugin; raises an exception when the provider is not enabled.
api.has_service(name) / api.list_services()Checks whether a service exists / lists all services.
api.register_content_provider(kind, provider_id, handler)Registers a content source; with kind="poem" the returned text replaces the built-in poems. The callback receives {"levels": [...]}.
api.register_weather_provider(provider_id, display_name, handler)Registers a weather source, which appears in the "Settings → Global → Weather Source" dropdown; the callback receives the city name and returns weather text.
api.register_settings_page(page_id, display_name, widget_class)Registers an entry on the settings page in the form of a button; clicking it opens the plugin page in a separate window.
api.register_card_slot(slot_id, display_name, widget_class, anchor="bottom", size=(320,120), offset=(0,0))Embeds a widget around the countdown card. anchor accepts top/bottom/left/right and corner combinations; size and offset are in pixels.
api.register_project_type(type_id, name, description="")Registers a new project type, which then appears in the type dropdown of "new project" and the project editor.

Available hooks: project_create, project_save, timer_start, timer_pause, timer_reset, timer_expire, window_close, theme_change, config_change and app_quit. Returning deny can block the matching operation (only on hooks that allow interception).

A plugin placed next to demo.py may ship a demo.json manifest with these optional fields: name, version, author, description, permissions (bit mask, legacy), permissions_v2 (baseline and on_demand), own_modules (allowlist of the plugin's own modules), api_version (loading is refused when it exceeds the current plugin API version) and requires (names of plugin files it depends on; load order is sorted automatically and a missing dependency causes the plugin to be skipped). Each entry of on_demand under permissions_v2 is a dictionary: {"perm": "NETWORK", "feature": "云同步", "title": "云同步需要访问网络", "reason": "…", "fallback": true}; fallback only applies to network and clipboard.

Callbacks a plugin class may implement: on_enable, on_disable, on_window_create(window, project), on_window_closed(window, project) and on_settings_closed().

Every registration method verifies that widget_class inherits from QWidget and checks id_name for duplicates; a duplicate raises ValueError.

🧩 API additions in 4.3.0

CapabilityDetails
permissions_v2 / on_demandRecommended form: put baseline permissions in baseline and declare advanced ones in on_demand (perm, feature, title, reason; fallback is valid for network and clipboard). Only permissions listed in on_demand can be requested with request_permission.
api.request_permission(perm, feature, reason, timeout_ms)Requests one permission when the user invokes an advanced feature and returns a PermissionResult usable as a boolean. Grant levels are once, session and permanent; after deny-and-remember, permission_status returns "deny".
api.register_card_slot(...)Embeds a widget on the top, bottom, left, right or a corner of the countdown card with pixel size and offset.
api.register_float_widget(...)Registers a desktop floating widget listed under independent widgets in the window context menu.
api.register_fullscreen_skin(...)Registers a fullscreen skin. It appears only in the fullscreen background selector and is no longer duplicated into dynamic backgrounds or the project window background dropdown.
api.hook(name, callback, priority)Subscribes to a hook; the callback may return allow, modify or deny. Hooks: project_create, project_save, timer_start, timer_pause, timer_reset, timer_expire, window_close, theme_change, config_change, app_quit.
api.register_action(scope, id, label, callback, icon)Registers an action in window_menu, tray_menu or settings_toolbar.
api.register_project_type(id, name, description)Registers a project type shown in the new-project and project editor type dropdowns.
api.register_content_provider(kind, id, handler)Registers a content provider; kind="poem" replaces the built-in poem source.
api.register_weather_provider(id, name, handler)Registers a weather provider shown in the global weather source dropdown.
api.provide_service(name, handler) / call_service / has_service / list_servicesPublishes and calls cross-plugin services; both sides need PLUGIN_CALL.
api.bind_behavior(cls, name, func)Rewrites widget class behavior; requires UI_MUTATE.
api.describe(obj) / members(obj) / signature(func)Safe introspection without importing inspect.
api.host.slots() / api.host.theme() / api.host.windows_meta()The plugin subprocess reads real slot, theme and window data through a host request/reply channel; requires UI_READ.
api.ping()Returns host PID, public version, build number and plugin API version for connectivity checks; requires SYSTEM_INFO.
api.registry_read(path, name=None, root="HKEY_CURRENT_USER") / registry_write / registry_deleteThe host performs registry access; requires REGISTRY. Only the Software subtree is allowed; writes and deletes are limited to HKCU, while HKLM is read-only.
api.run_command(command, timeout_ms)The host runs a system command and returns the exit code and output; requires COMMAND.
api.spawn_process(program, args, timeout_ms, cwd)The host launches an external program and returns the exit code and output; requires PROCESS_SPAWN.
api.socket_probe(host, port, timeout_ms)The host performs one TCP connect probe; requires NETWORK_SOCKET.

Not provided: COMMAND_EXEC has no plugin-side wrapper and plugins cannot import subprocess. It is equivalent to launching arbitrary executables and is riskier than controlled command execution; use api.spawn_process with PROCESS_SPAWN instead.

Cross-plugin data: PLUGIN_DATA_SHARE is reserved as a permission bit only. This version has no exports.data file sharing interface; use api.provide_service / api.call_service for cross-plugin communication.

items.title: Complete Plugin Example
items.html:
💡 Complete Plugin Example: Classroom Bell Card

This plugin walks through the full workflow recommended by the current version: a v2 manifest with permissions, the plugin class, a card slot, a settings page, persisted configuration, an on-demand notification permission, and dark/light theme adaptation. Put both files into the plugins folder and enable the plugin in Plugin Management.

1. Manifest: classroom_bell.json

{
  "name": "课堂提醒",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "author": "YourName",
  "description": "在倒计时卡片下方显示距离上课的剩余时间，并支持到点通知",
  "api_version": 2,
  "own_modules": ["classroom_bell.py"],
  "permissions_v2": {
    "baseline": ["UI_INJECT"],
    "on_demand": [
      {
        "perm": "NOTIFICATION",
        "feature": "到点提醒",
        "title": "到点弹出一条系统通知",
        "reason": "在设定的上课时间到达前，通过系统通知提醒一次"
      }
    ]
  }
}
  • api_version: loading is refused when it exceeds the plugin API version supported by the host; the current value is 2.
  • baseline: confirmed once at enable time. Registering card slots and settings pages requires UI_INJECT.
  • on_demand: only permissions declared here can ever produce a request_permission prompt.
  • own_modules: declares the plugin's own module files so reading them is not treated as reading another plugin's source.

2. Plugin: classroom_bell.py

from datetime import datetime, timedelta

from PyQt6.QtCore import QTime, QTimer
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import (QCheckBox, QHBoxLayout, QLabel, QPushButton,
                             QSpinBox, QTimeEdit, QVBoxLayout, QWidget)

from djs_pyqt6 import Plugin, PluginPermission, Theme, get_theme_colors

APP = None
API = None


def colors():
    theme = getattr(APP, "theme", None)
    if theme is None:
        theme = Theme()
    return get_theme_colors(theme)


def style():
    return (
        "QWidget { background: %(panel_bg)s; color: %(text_color)s; }"
        "QLabel#BellTitle { color: %(secondary_text)s; font-size: 12px; }"
        "QLabel#BellValue { color: %(accent)s; font-size: 26px; font-weight: 700; }"
        "QLabel#BellHint { color: %(secondary_text)s; font-size: 12px; }"
        "QTimeEdit, QSpinBox { background: %(input_bg)s; color: %(text_color)s;"
        " border: 1px solid %(border_color)s; border-radius: 5px; padding: 4px 6px; }"
        "QCheckBox { color: %(text_color)s; }"
        "QPushButton { background: %(accent)s; color: %(btn_text)s; border: none;"
        " border-radius: 6px; padding: 7px 14px; }"
        % colors()
    )


def target_time():
    start = int(API.get_config("start_min", 480))
    now = datetime.now()
    target = now.replace(hour=start // 60 % 24, minute=start % 60,
                         second=0, microsecond=0)
    if target <= now:
        target += timedelta(days=1)
    return target


class BellCard(QWidget):
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        layout = QVBoxLayout(self)
        layout.setContentsMargins(16, 12, 16, 12)
        layout.setSpacing(2)
        self.title = QLabel("课堂提醒", self)
        self.title.setObjectName("BellTitle")
        self.value = QLabel("--:--", self)
        self.value.setObjectName("BellValue")
        self.hint = QLabel("", self)
        self.hint.setObjectName("BellHint")
        layout.addWidget(self.title)
        layout.addWidget(self.value)
        layout.addWidget(self.hint)
        self.fired = ""
        self.styled = ""
        self.timer = QTimer(self)
        self.timer.setInterval(1000)
        self.timer.timeout.connect(self.refresh)
        self.timer.start()
        self.refresh()

    def refresh(self):
        sheet = style()
        if sheet != self.styled:
            self.styled = sheet
            self.setStyleSheet(sheet)
        target = target_time()
        remain = max(0, int((target - datetime.now()).total_seconds()))
        if remain >= 3600:
            self.value.setText("%d:%02d:%02d" % (remain // 3600, remain % 3600 // 60,
                                                 remain % 60))
        else:
            self.value.setText("%02d:%02d" % (remain // 60, remain % 60))
        self.hint.setText("距离 %s 上课" % target.strftime("%H:%M"))
        remind = max(0, int(API.get_config("remind_min", 10))) * 60
        key = target.strftime("%Y%m%d%H%M")
        if 0 < remain <= remind and self.fired != key:
            self.fired = key
            API.log("课堂提醒触发：%s 上课" % target.strftime("%H:%M"))
            if bool(API.get_config("notify", False)):
                try:
                    API.show_notification("课堂提醒",
                                          "%s 上课，请做好准备" % target.strftime("%H:%M"))
                except PermissionError:
                    API.set_config("notify", False)
                    API.log("通知权限已失效，改为只在卡片上提醒", "WARNING")


class BellSettings(QWidget):
    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        layout = QVBoxLayout(self)
        layout.setContentsMargins(20, 18, 20, 18)
        layout.setSpacing(10)
        title = QLabel("课堂提醒设置", self)
        font = title.font()
        font.setBold(True)
        font.setPointSize(14)
        title.setFont(font)
        layout.addWidget(title)
        row = QHBoxLayout()
        row.addWidget(QLabel("上课时间", self))
        self.edit_time = QTimeEdit(self)
        self.edit_time.setDisplayFormat("HH:mm")
        row.addWidget(self.edit_time)
        row.addStretch(1)
        layout.addLayout(row)
        row = QHBoxLayout()
        row.addWidget(QLabel("提前提醒", self))
        self.spin_remind = QSpinBox(self)
        self.spin_remind.setRange(0, 60)
        self.spin_remind.setSuffix(" 分钟")
        row.addWidget(self.spin_remind)
        row.addStretch(1)
        layout.addLayout(row)
        self.chk_notify = QCheckBox("到点弹出系统通知", self)
        layout.addWidget(self.chk_notify)
        self.status = QLabel("", self)
        self.status.setWordWrap(True)
        layout.addWidget(self.status)
        layout.addStretch(1)
        self.btn_save = QPushButton("保存", self)
        self.btn_save.clicked.connect(self.save)
        layout.addWidget(self.btn_save)
        start = int(API.get_config("start_min", 480))
        self.edit_time.setTime(QTime(start // 60 % 24, start % 60))
        self.spin_remind.setValue(int(API.get_config("remind_min", 10)))
        self.chk_notify.setChecked(bool(API.get_config("notify", False)))
        self.setStyleSheet(style())

    def save(self):
        notify = self.chk_notify.isChecked()
        message = "已保存，卡片会立即按新设置倒计时。"
        if notify and not API.request_permission(
                PluginPermission.NOTIFICATION, "到点提醒",
                "在设定的上课时间到达前，通过系统通知提醒一次"):
            notify = False
            self.chk_notify.setChecked(False)
            message = "未获得通知权限，已改为只在卡片上提醒。"
        value = self.edit_time.time()
        API.set_config("start_min", value.hour() * 60 + value.minute())
        API.set_config("remind_min", self.spin_remind.value())
        API.set_config("notify", notify)
        self.status.setText(message)
        API.log("课堂提醒设置已保存")


class ClassroomBellPlugin(Plugin):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.name = "课堂提醒"
        self.version = "1.0.0"
        self.author = "YourName"
        self.description = "显示距离上课的剩余时间，并支持到点通知"

    def on_enable(self):
        self.api.register_card_slot("classroom_bell_card", "课堂提醒卡片",
                                    BellCard, "bottom", (320, 96), (0, -8))
        self.api.register_settings_page("classroom_bell_page", "课堂提醒设置",
                                        BellSettings, (420, 360))
        self.api.log("课堂提醒已启用")

    def on_disable(self):
        self.api.log("课堂提醒已停用")


def setup(app, api):
    global APP, API
    APP = app
    API = api
    return ClassroomBellPlugin()

The UI strings stay in Chinese, matching the rest of the application; replace them with your own text if you prefer.

3. How it runs

  1. Drop both files into the plugins folder, open Settings → Plugin Management and enable "课堂提醒". Only the baseline UI_INJECT permission is confirmed at this point.
  2. A "课堂提醒" card appears below the countdown card and refreshes the time left until class every second.
  3. Open "课堂提醒设置" from the plugin details to adjust the class time and the lead minutes, then tick "到点弹出系统通知".
  4. NOTIFICATION is requested on demand only when the box is ticked and saved. If it is denied, the plugin falls back to card-only reminders without raising an error.
  5. Settings are persisted in the plugin configuration and survive a restart. Colors come from get_theme_colors, so both light and dark themes are supported.

4. Key points

  • Widget classes must inherit QWidget and provide a parent=None default; the host instantiates them as cls().
  • Never touch host windows: a plugin runs in its own subprocess and communicates only through api; app exposes only read-only values such as data_dir and theme.
  • Callback arguments must be JSON-serializable; QWidget and QObject instances are not allowed.
  • Degrade on denied permissions: turn the toggle off and show an inline status instead of surfacing an exception.
  • Use api.get_config / api.set_config for configuration instead of writing files yourself.
  • The plugin constructor takes no app/api arguments. They arrive through setup(app, api) and self.api, which is the biggest difference from older examples.

items.title: Signing and Security (Deprecated)
items.html:
🔑 Plugin Signature Verification (Advanced Security)

To ensure that plugins come from a trusted source, the app supports Ed25519 signature verification. A developer can generate a signature file (.py.sig) for a plugin file (.py); once a user enables signature verification, only plugins with a valid signature are loaded.

Signature verification is off by default and ordinary users do not need to worry about it. Developers who want to use it should study the _verify_signature method in the source code.

items.title: Sandbox and Auditing
items.html:
🛡️ Plugin Sandbox and Auditing

  • Sandbox: Plugins run in a restricted Python environment where __builtins__ is replaced with a safe subset and dangerous functions such as open, eval and exec are intercepted by the audit hook.
  • Audit hook: sys.addaudithook monitors every sensitive operation (files, network, commands). Unauthorised operations raise PermissionError and are written to the "Sensitive Operations" log. Interception decisions and log switches are independent: turning off "详细记录放行的敏感操作" only reduces allowed records, it does not loosen interception.
  • Unknown origin: If a sensitive operation comes from code in a plugin directory but cannot be matched to a specific plugin instance (for example, a string run through exec, or a call wrapped by a third-party library), it is rejected and logged as coming from an "unknown plugin" rather than being silently allowed. The app's own file operations use a separate allowlist and are unaffected.
  • Interception hints and aggregation: When something is blocked, a manageable card appears in the lower-right corner. Its top-left corner carries the source marker (a dedicated icon + the app name + "Security Center"), making clear that the hint comes from this app's Security Center and not from a system notification; when the window is narrow the text shrinks to "Security Center" while the icon always remains. The same plugin, operation and reason are shown only once within the cooldown, every card has a close button in its top-right corner and closes itself after 12 seconds. When the same plugin, operation and reason occurs twice or more within one second, or three or more interceptions from any source accumulate within one second, the interface merges them into a single "已自动处理 N 项" summary card whose title and detail count grow in real time as new interceptions arrive; "展开明细" lists the plugin, time and reason for each entry, and the close button clears every detail collected in that merge.
  • Logging: Every plugin operation is written to the log file data/LOG.txt and to the log area in the interface, which makes troubleshooting easier.

items.title: Plugin Security Center (8 Tabs)
items.html:
🧭 Plugin Security Center (8 Tabs)

The Security Center gathers plugin-related records and actions into 8 tabs. Every record page supports keyword filtering and sorting by time or plugin, and double-clicking any row opens its details with the plugin, event, target, decision reason and time.

What the Eight Tabs Are For

  • Interception records: Operations rejected by the audit hook. The "decision reason" in the details explains whether a permission was missing, a "Deny and remember" rule matched, or the path was outside the allowlist.
  • Allowed records: Operations that passed auditing. Entries accumulate only while "详细记录放行的敏感操作" is on; once it is off no new entries appear, and interception is unaffected.
  • File operations: Plugin reads, writes, deletions and renames, with path and result, so you can check whether a plugin touched files it should not.
  • Plugin permission management: Grants viewed from two angles — by plugin, which lists each plugin's current grant levels, and by permission, which lists which plugins hold each permission.
  • Sensitive records: The raw sensitive-operation stream, kept in chronological order with full text, for cross-checking the first three record pages.
  • Plugin log: Log output the plugin itself produces through the API, for debugging its internal logic.
  • Protection management: Master switches and record policy — whether auditing is enabled, whether allowed operations are recorded, whether the Security Center may be closed and so on.
  • Trust mode: Enable or revoke trust mode for an individual plugin; independent of the four grant levels.

Four Grant Levels and Lifetimes

Every permission in the permission manager can be set to one of these levels:

  • Not granted: Nothing is granted and the operation is blocked; no persistent exception is created.
  • Allow once: Expires as soon as this call succeeds, and the next identical operation is blocked again. Use it to temporarily allow a suspicious but necessary operation.
  • This session: Valid for the lifetime of the current process and expires when the app exits; after a restart it reverts to Not granted.
  • Always allow: Written to the configuration file and valid after restarts until revoked manually.
  • Deny and remember: Written to the configuration and rejected directly in the audit hook; it overrides any other level that previously granted the permission, and revoking it restores the previous behaviour.

Grant details are stored under grants_v2 in data/plugin_security.json, while the permission bit map is only a runtime cache. They can be changed from either the grant dialog or "Plugin permission management" in the Security Center; saving in either place takes effect immediately and syncs to the plugin host process.

Using the Summary Card

When the same plugin, operation and reason occurs twice or more within one second, or three or more interceptions from any source accumulate within one second, the individual hints in the lower-right corner merge into a single "已自动处理 N 项" summary card. Its title and detail count keep growing as new interceptions arrive, even while the details are expanded; "展开明细" lets you read each entry, and the close button clears every detail collected in that merge. In single-card mode the close button and cooldown still work as before.

Where to Add an Allowlist Entry

Select a record on the "Interception records" or "File operations" page and click "加入白名单" to add that record's target path to the plugin's path allowlist; the same action is available in the record details dialog. The allowlist is stored per "plugin + path" and applies to that plugin only. Afterwards the plugin's access to the same path is allowed directly, although "Deny and remember" and the program's protected files still apply. Remove allowlist entries from the details dialog or the permission management page.

Source Marker and Dedicated Icon

The Security Center uses a dedicated vector icon: a shield outline containing a centred monitoring ring and a solid node, representing continuous monitoring of local plugin activity and distinguishing it from the usual generic shield; at 16 pixels and below only the shield and the centre dot are kept so the outline stays intact at small sizes. The icon appears in the top-left corner of interception hint cards, in the Security Center window title bar, on the Security Center entry button in Settings Center and on this help page's navigation entry, and its colour follows the current theme with one variant for dark and one for light.
