The interception hint card in the lower-right corner shows "app name + Security Center" as its source text in the top-left corner, with a font size and colour subordinate to the main title; when the available width is insufficient it shrinks to "Security Center" and the icon is never dropped. Seeing that marker confirms the hint comes from this app's Security Center.

items.title: Permission Best Practices
items.html:
📜 Plugin Permission Best Practices

  • Least privilege: A plugin should request only the permissions it genuinely needs. A weather plugin, for example, needs network access and nothing else; it should not ask for file write access.
  • User confirmation: When a plugin is enabled, the user sees a permission request dialog, so explain clearly why each permission is needed.
  • Regular audits: Users are advised to review the plugin list and sensitive-operation records from time to time, and to disable a plugin promptly if anything looks wrong.

items.title: Sensitive Operation Audit
items.html:
📝 Sensitive Operation Audit

The "Sensitive Operations" tab in the plugin manager records the details of every file, network and command call made by each plugin. For example:

[2025-01-15 10:30:22] [StockPlugin] 网络访问 | GET https://api.example.com/stock

This helps users understand what a plugin does and spot potentially malicious behaviour. If a plugin repeatedly tries to reach resources it does not need, consider disabling it or tightening its permissions.

items.title: Debug Console Guide
items.html:
🐞 Debug Console Guide

Press ~ or ` on the keyboard while the settings interface is open to bring up the built-in debug console. It is an interactive Python environment with command history, Tab completion and 20+ built-in debugging commands.

Interface

  • Log forwarding switch: A checkbox in the toolbar, off by default so logs do not flood the output. When enabled, system logs appear in the console in real time.
  • ↑↓ arrow keys: Browse command history so you can repeat earlier commands easily.
  • Tab key: Completes command names — type the first few letters and press Tab.
  • Clear / Help buttons: Clear the screen or list every command in one click.

Built-in Commands

CommandArgumentsDescription
help-Shows the complete list of commands with help text
clear-Clears the console output
restart-Restarts the whole application
clear_cache-Clears app caches (weather, background and other temporary data)
perf_info-Shows performance statistics: window count, thread count, memory usage
theme_info-Shows details of the current theme (name, colour values, mode)
app_info-Shows the app version, Python version and system environment
list_threads-Lists all active threads and their states
backup_config-Backs up the current configuration file into the backups/ directory
open_settings-Opens the Global Settings window quickly
toggle_log-Toggles log forwarding (on/off)
close_window<N>Closes the Nth floating window (numbered from 0)
list_windows-Lists the index and name of every floating window
show_windows-Shows all floating windows
hide_windows-Hides all floating windows
set_window_alpha<0.1-1.0>Sets the global opacity of all windows
list_projects-Lists every project name and target date
dump_project<N>Prints the complete configuration (JSON) of the Nth project
reload_theme-Reloads the theme stylesheet
plugins-Lists every loaded plugin
enable_plugin<name>Enables the plugin with the given name
disable_plugin<name>Disables the plugin with the given name
set_debug_level<0-3>Sets the global debug level (0 = off, 1 = errors, 2 = info, 3 = verbose)
refresh_weather-Forces a weather refresh for all windows
exit-Closes the debug console window

Advanced Usage

The console evaluates any Python expression; type it and press Enter to run it. For example:

len(app.windows)          # 查看当前悬浮窗数量
app.theme.is_dark          # 检查是否为暗色主题
app.projects[0].name       # 查看第一个项目的名称
[x.project.name for x in app.windows]  # 列表推导式

If a command is not built in, the console tries to evaluate it with eval(), so you can reach any object attribute or method rooted at app.

Notes

  • Log forwarding is off by default, so command output is not drowned out by log traffic.
  • Commands that change app state (such as set_window_alpha or set_debug_level) take effect immediately.
  • restart closes all windows and reloads the app; make sure your work is saved first.
  • close_window N permanently removes the matching floating window, and the action cannot be undone.

items.title: Log Levels and Viewing Logs
items.html:
📄 Log Levels and How to View Logs

The log level can be adjusted in Global Settings:

  • 0 - Off: Nothing is logged
  • 1 - Errors/Warnings: Only errors and warnings are logged
  • 2 - Info: General information is logged (the default)
  • 3 - Verbose: Everything is logged, including the details of plugin calls

The log file is data/LOG.txt, and the "查看日志文件" button opens it quickly. Each entry records the time, level, call site and content, which helps with troubleshooting.

items.title: Window and Countdown Issues
items.html:
❔ Window and Countdown Issues

  • The window will not move: Hold the left button on any empty part of the window to drag; buttons, progress bars and other interactive controls keep their own interaction, and the edges/corners resize. A window may be dragged at most half its width or height off-screen, so at least half stays visible; the tray menu item "重置窗口位置" still recentres it.
  • The countdown is not updating: Check whether the target date has passed — an expired project shows "已到期". When the workday count is 0 the static text may be empty, but the numeric countdown should still update. Also check the log file for errors.
  • Digit rolling looks choppy: Digit animation uses QPropertyAnimation and is normally smooth. If it stutters, the dynamic wallpaper is probably using too much; lower the frame rate or quality.
  • Some screens keep their old colours after switching light/dark: Switch through Settings Center → Global Settings → "深浅色主题"; the app rebuilds the settings interface automatically. If you chose "Follow System", confirm that the Windows "应用模式" really did change, then wait about 2 seconds for it to sync.
  • Text is hard to read in dark mode: Floating-window text colour belongs to the project skin, so adjust it in the skin editor; interface widget text is coloured by the theme automatically.

items.title: Weather and Network Issues
items.html:
❔ Weather Widget and Network Issues

  • No weather is shown: First confirm that you are online. QWeather (和风天气) requires you to open your own account and fill in your API Key/Host (Global Settings → Weather Source; click "📖 如何开通和风天气 API" for the guide). Until it is configured, the widget reports "未配置和风天气 API Key". A custom URL template is also an option.
  • The city name shows as pinyin: For a few cities the QWeather GeoAPI returns pinyin in its name field.
  • Clicking the weather label does nothing: A successful weather fetch is needed first, because the forecast window requires latitude and longitude. If fetching keeps failing, check the log.
  • Update check?: That feature cannot be implemented for now.

items.title: Plugin Troubleshooting
items.html:
❔ Plugin Loading or Runtime Failures

  • The plugin list is empty: Confirm that the plugins folder exists and contains .py files, and that the global plugin system is on (the switch on the Plugins page).
  • "权限不足" appears when enabling a plugin: The permission the plugin requested was not granted to the user; add it manually in the permission manager.
  • Plugin failed to load (syntax error): Check the plugin log or the console output, fix the plugin code and restart the app.
  • A plugin crashes the app: If one plugin causes a crash, start in safe mode: delete or move that plugin file out, then restart. Alternatively launch with the command-line argument --no-plugins (you will need to implement it yourself).

items.title: Dynamic Wallpaper Performance
items.html:
❔ Dynamic Wallpaper Stutter or Performance Problems

  • Enable GPU shader acceleration (experimental): Tick "实验性：GPU 着色器加速" under Global Settings → Render Backend; Aurora / Sky then render on the GPU with OpenGL Compatibility Profile + GLSL
  • Lower the frame rate: Dropping from 60 FPS to 30 FPS noticeably reduces CPU/GPU load.
  • Lower the quality: Choosing "Low" reduces the number of particles and stars. Aurora / Sky (whether GPU or CPU rendered) downgrade automatically based on frame time (quality or frame rate) and ramp back up when performance recovers. At low quality the GPU shader uses fewer FBM octaves and fewer clouds and skips light-beam computation.
  • Turn the dynamic wallpaper off: On lower-end hardware, prefer a static image or a solid colour background.
  • Mouse Particles mode: This mode has many particles and heavy line computation, so it demands more performance — especially with CPU fallback rendering.
  • Render pausing: GL rendering pauses automatically while a context menu, combo box or layout editor dialog is in use; hovering over a panel drops it to 12 FPS and moving away restores it.

items.title: Mouse Cheat Sheet
items.html:
🖱️ Mouse Cheat Sheet

  • Left-drag in the centre → move the window
  • Left-drag an edge/corner → resize
  • Right-click → context menu
  • Double-click → open settings
  • In fullscreen mode, move the pointer to the bottom-right corner → show the control panel
  • Standalone floating widgets: drag to move, wheel to scale, drag an edge or corner to resize, right-click for the menu
  • Pomodoro: click to start/pause, double-click to reset the current phase, use the context menu to change phase

items.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
items.html:
⌨️ Keyboard Shortcuts

  • While the settings interface is open, press ~ or ` → open the debug console
  • In fullscreen mode there are currently no preset keyboard shortcuts; use the mouse control panel instead.

items.title: Productivity Tips
items.html:
💡 Productivity Tips

  • Duplicating a project quickly: There is no "Duplicate Project" button yet, but you can edit a project by hand and then copy its block in the configuration file (carefully).
  • Backing up the configuration: In Settings Center, the "Backup Config" button archives the current configuration into data/backups/ in one click, and "Restore Config" restores from a backup (a restart is needed for the restore to take effect).
  • Custom poems: Edit data/poems.json and add lines you like in the existing format.
  • Keeping a window on top: Use "Pin Window" in the context menu to keep the window above other applications at all times.
  • Desktop decoration: Combining "Pin Window" with "Click-Through" keeps the countdown on the desktop without blocking anything. See [[ref:click-through]].
  • Recurring reminders: Setting the project type to "Recurring" gives you periodic countdowns for weekly meetings, daily check-ins and so on. See [[ref:loop-settings]].

items.title: Version Information
items.html:
🆕 What's new in 4.5.5

  • Project home moved to Gitee and GitHub: Check for updates in Settings now offers both Gitee and GitHub project pages, and Feature vote opens the Gitee repository's Issues page.
  • Remote consoles updated: the Windows console settings and the Android console settings now list both Gitee and GitHub project pages.
  • Plugin authors need no changes: this release only updates project links; the manifest and API are unchanged.

🆕 What's new in 4.5.4

  • Complete plugin example rewritten: the “Complete Plugin Example” topic now uses a runnable Classroom Bell plugin covering a v2 manifest, card slots, a settings page, persisted configuration, an on-demand notification permission and light/dark theme support. Outdated patterns from the old sample, such as registering a QLabel as a dynamic background or passing app/api into the plugin constructor, are gone.
  • Plugin authors need no changes: the manifest structure and API are unchanged; this release only updates the help content.

🆕 What's new in 4.5.3

  • Spin arrow direction fixed: the up and down buttons overlapped because percentage heights were not applied, so both only increased the value; each button now has its own area and works correctly.
  • Floating widgets are resizable: hover the edge or corner of a floating widget, then drag the resize cursor to change its size; the size is saved automatically.
  • New spin-box arrows: up/down arrows now sit in a dedicated thin column with reserved space on the right, so they never cover digits.
  • Font settings fixed with previews: countdown digits now honor the chosen font. Each entry in the font list renders “测试 Test” in its own typeface with the family name beside it.
  • Image background survives restart: applying a custom background in the skin editor no longer gets overwritten by the skin snapshot on the next launch; the saved image stays after closing and reopening.

🆕 What's new in 4.4.0

  • Network time sync: Global settings now include “Network time sync”. The clock is calibrated at startup and every 30 minutes, and the offset and source are shown in settings. Countdowns, loops and expiry checks use the calibrated time with second-level accuracy.
  • Countdown accuracy audit: targets are parsed by minute and recomputed every 250 ms from the calibrated clock, keeping display error below one second without drift.
  • Floating widgets can be removed: plugin widgets now expose “Remove this widget” in their context menu, and the host deletes the instance and its configuration.
  • Hide all windows covers floating widgets: hiding all windows also hides schedule widgets, and showing all windows restores them.
  • Plugin settings pages can declare a default size: api.register_settings_page(id, name, cls, (width, height)) sets the opening window size and is clamped to the available screen area; without it the previous 640×420 is used.
  • Plugin authors: call api.remove_float_widget(widget) if a widget should remove itself; no manifest changes are required.

Data directory: {data_dir}

🆕 What's new in 4.3.14

  • Fixed the fullscreen plugin background showing white with no plugin visuals: plugin backgrounds render in a host process, and their native window covered every painted element while being hidden by the translucent countdown window when embedded as a child; the plugin background now lives in its own backdrop window below the countdown window, so countdown text and controls overlay it correctly.
  • Fixed the fullscreen control panel not reappearing after fading out: once fully transparent the panel could no longer receive pointer-enter events; the pointer position is now polled and entering the panel area restores it.
  • Plugin authors need no changes: no manifest or plugin code updates are required.

🆕 What's new in 4.3.13

  • Fixed the fullscreen control panel not coming back after fading out: plugin backgrounds are separate native windows that covered the panel embedded in the countdown window, so the pointer could never enter it after it faded; the panel is now a separate always-on-top window that stays above the background and reappears on hover.
  • Plugin authors need no changes: no manifest or plugin code updates are required.

🆕 What's new in 4.3.12

  • Fixed the fullscreen window being shifted to the middle of the screen: at the moment fullscreen was entered, the off-screen guard treated the old position combined with the new size as out of bounds and moved the window, leaving it away from the top-left corner with only part of the content visible; fullscreen windows now skip the bounds correction.
  • Plugin authors need no changes: no manifest or plugin code updates are required.

🆕 What's new in 4.3.11

  • Fixed the fullscreen window jumping to one side: a leftover drag state from before the transition kept treating mouse moves as window dragging, pulling the fullscreen window away from the top-left corner so only a clipped corner stayed visible; entering fullscreen now clears drag and resize state, and window dragging is disabled while fullscreen.
  • No window geometry write-back while fullscreen: saving configuration now skips the window position and size while fullscreen, so the fullscreen size is not stored as the normal window size.
  • Plugin authors need no changes: no manifest or plugin code updates are required.

🆕 What's new in 4.3.10

  • Fixed plugin fullscreen background position and size: plugin backgrounds render in the host process, and after embedding the top-left position and size were not synchronized, so the content shrank into the bottom-right corner with blank space around it; embedding now aligns the window to the background layer and keeps it in sync on resize.
  • Plugin background window is released when leaving fullscreen: exiting fullscreen or switching backgrounds now detaches the host control immediately, leaving no stray window behind.
  • Plugin background preview no longer shows loading: the fullscreen appearance list now shows a static hint image for plugin backgrounds and only creates the real background after entering fullscreen; plugin backgrounds also hide the ineffective quality presets.
  • No plugin changes required: no manifest or plugin code updates needed.

🆕 What's new in 4.3.9

  • Fixed a crash when using the fullscreen appearance dialog: the main window global mouse filter called window() on objects directly, but dialogs such as the fullscreen appearance dialog keep window as their own attribute, which raised TypeError and terminated the app; the check now falls back safely, so clicking and dragging inside those dialogs no longer crashes.
  • No plugin changes required: no manifest or plugin code updates needed.

🆕 What's new in 4.3.8

  • Log storms no longer crowd out control events: when a plugin produces a burst of logs, only log and security records are throttled; window creation and registration events are still handled, so plugin windows no longer stay at loading next to a separate window.
  • Embedding retries automatically: if the embed message does not take effect after the host creates the window, it keeps retrying until embedding succeeds or the limit is reached.
  • No manifest changes: this is a host event dispatch fix.

🆕 What's new in 4.3.7

  • Plugin UI follows permissions: revoking UI injection hides the plugin's settings page and panel entries immediately and closes any open page window, so a page can no longer stay open while its widget fails to load.
  • Widget creation failures are reported: when the host refuses to create a widget, the real reason and a hint are shown instead of an endless loading placeholder.
  • No manifest changes: this is a UI/permission linkage fix.

🆕 What's new in 4.3.6

  • Revoking grants now applies inside the plugin host: after the main process clears or revokes a plugin's grants, the host receives an empty snapshot and deletes the old permanent records instead of keeping stale permissions.
  • File and clipboard access are blocked again: with all permissions turned off, file reads, clipboard reads and similar operations are intercepted and logged in the Security Center; active grants are withdrawn immediately without restarting.
  • No manifest changes: this is an authorization sync fix.

🆕 What's new in 4.3.5

  • No leftovers after disabling: once a plugin is disabled, its context-menu and tray actions, project types, weather sources, settings page tabs, plugin panels, dynamic backgrounds and fullscreen skins are removed from the interface immediately; a background in use falls back to the default starfield and the weather source falls back to QWeather.
  • No new plugin widgets while disabled: the host refuses to create windows for a disabled plugin, so leftover entry points can no longer open plugin UI.
  • Re-enabling restores everything: actions, project types, weather sources, settings pages and card slots come back after enabling the plugin again, without restarting the app.
  • Plugin authors: no changes needed: this release only cleans up the disable lifecycle; manifests stay as they are.

🆕 What's new in 4.3.4

  • Floating widgets appear again: desktop widgets of unknown or disabled plugin types no longer leave a placeholder window behind; they are created once the plugin registers, so adding one is visible immediately.
  • The lower half drags again: mouse drags over plugin card slots and plugin floating widgets are forwarded from the plugin host to the main process, so whole-window dragging works while plugin buttons stay clickable.
  • Cursor and smoothness restored: plugin details in Settings now open in a separate window instead of embedding a cross-process native widget, restoring the open animation, click response and overall smoothness.
  • Sturdier host startup: host output is drained continuously to keep the log pipe clear, a failed handshake retries once with the last output logged, and early startup saves no longer wipe enabled plugin states.
  • Feedback when adding: adding a widget whose plugin is disabled now shows a message instead of doing nothing.
  • Plugin authors: no action needed: this release fixes host interaction and window lifecycle; the manifest is unchanged.

🆕 What's new in 4.3.3

  • Drag from anywhere: the countdown window drags from any point, not only the upper half; buttons, progress bars, inputs and lists keep their own interaction, while edges and corners still resize.
  • Bounds apply to every window: the on-screen guard now covers every top-level window the app creates, including floating widgets, the settings window and dialogs.
  • Half off-screen allowed: a window may be dragged out by at most half of its width or height, so at least half stays visible and it cannot be lost.
  • No plugin changes needed: host interaction and window behaviour only.

🆕 What's new in 4.3.2

  • Permission prompts no longer freeze plugins: The plugin host keeps processing widget events while it waits for the decision, so plugin windows stay paint-able and usable until the answer arrives.
  • Plugins stay responsive while loading: The host now yields to the event loop between plugins, so windows being dragged keep their embedded content in sync.
  • Widget placeholders no longer stick: Widget creation is retried when the host is not yet connected or busy, and repeated requests for the same token reuse the existing window instead of stacking extra ones.
  • Plugin panels and settings pages are owned by the settings window: Reopening reuses a single window instead of creating overlapping duplicates.
  • Card slots work again: Fixed the registry lookup so plugin-registered card slots embed in the main window.
  • No manifest changes required: This release fixes host behaviour only.

🆕 What's new in 4.3.1

  • Host capabilities bind the caller identity: When a plugin runs a restricted capability through a host request, the host decides permissions from the plugin currently being dispatched instead of trusting the plugin name in the request payload, so a plugin without a grant can no longer impersonate one that has it for registry, command, process or socket operations.
  • api.ping() is permission-checked: The connectivity check returns the host PID and version, so it now requires SYSTEM_INFO and raises PluginPermissionDenied when undeclared instead of running unguarded.
  • Plugin authors need to act: Plugins that call api.ping() should add SYSTEM_INFO to permissions_v2.on_demand with a reason, otherwise the call is refused with a structured denial.

🆕 What's new in 4.3.0

  • Real host introspection: api.host.slots(), theme() and windows_meta() in the plugin subprocess now use a host request/reply channel and return real slots, theme and window data instead of empty values.
  • Plugin backgrounds in project windows: The project window background dropdown lists every registered plugin dynamic background and caps it at 30 FPS; fullscreen skins stay out of that list.
  • Plugin widgets can be added: The project layout editor's add-element dialog lists registered plugin widgets so they can be placed into a layout.
  • Plugin detail widgets: When a remote plugin implements get_info_widget(), the plugin detail page embeds the real widget from the host process.
  • Fullscreen skins split from dynamic backgrounds: Registering a fullscreen skin no longer duplicates it into the dynamic background table, and the fullscreen background selector still lists the skin.
  • New restricted system APIs: api.ping(), api.registry_read/write/delete(), api.run_command(), api.spawn_process() and api.socket_probe() are executed by the host and permission-checked.
  • Docs aligned with implementation: Removed the unimplemented exports.data sharing description, switched cross-plugin communication to public services, and documented that COMMAND_EXEC has no plugin-side wrapper.

🆕 What's new in 4.2.0

  • Interpreter guards block at the call site: Calls to sys.addaudithook, sys.settrace and sys.setprofile from a plugin frame now raise hard.security_hook immediately, so the log can no longer claim a block while the call actually succeeds.
  • Manager closed off: api._manager() returns a read-only facade; every attribute except _startup_dirs() raises hard.manager_access. Direct calls to set_grants_bulk, revoke_all_grants and grant_levels_snapshot are refused as well, so a plugin cannot grant itself permissions or read other plugins' grant details.
  • Autostart no longer switches auditing off: write_autostart_registry uses a one-shot token to allow the host's own write; a direct plugin call requires AUTOSTART and otherwise returns zone.startup or perm.not_granted.
  • The three suppression switches are unreachable from plugins: Writing _audit_suppress, _audit_guard.active or security_center_disabled from a plugin frame raises hard.audit_control or hard.app_control. The audit hook also only honours suppression for operations not started directly by a plugin, so even a bypassed attribute write is still audited.
  • Security event owners cannot be forged: append_security_event forces the owner to the real plugin found on the call stack, and clear_security_events rejects plugin calls with hard.audit_control.
  • Explanation gaps filled: Reading the main program source leaves an allow.app_source_read observation; import blocks are attributed to the calling plugin; host-mode api._app writes an api.direct_app_access observation; registry blocks record the concrete key path; zone.plugin_source denials carry the PLUGIN_SOURCE permission bit.
  • Behaviour changes to check: Plugins can no longer reach manager internals through api._manager(), set the three switches, write the autostart registry directly, or forge the owner of a security event; sys.settrace and sys.setprofile are refused inside a plugin frame. The regular api surface and the manifest structure are unchanged.

🆕 What's new in 4.1.4

  • Observations require a plugin frame: Observation events are recorded only when a plugin file frame exists in the call stack. Audit noise from the host's own startup, network access and the debug console no longer appears in the observation list, and interception decisions are unchanged.
  • Allow-once semantics fixed: A one-time grant returns to un-granted as soon as it is used, so the next request prompts again. Cancelling or closing the prompt no longer starts a cooldown, so a retry is possible immediately.
  • Prompt throttling is per permission: Requests for different permissions no longer consume each other's quota. The same permission can prompt at most 4 times per 60 seconds and returns rate_limited beyond that.
  • One-time grants no longer break mid-operation: Multiple audit events of the same operation (such as DNS lookup and connect) are no longer denied after the grant is consumed by the first event.
  • Clearer plugin logs: The test plugin now prints the result code for denied prompts, distinguishing user denial, throttling and missing grants.
  • Widget-class rewrites are now observed: When a plugin rewrites widget class attributes at runtime, the sealing mechanism no longer raises. It records an observe event named seal.widget_class with the attribute name as the target and a detail that states it is allowed in observation mode and will be blocked once tightened. The Security Center observation counter accumulates. Import-time rewrites are unchanged, and api.bind_behavior still requires UI_MUTATE.
  • Plugin compatibility: The manifest structure is unchanged; existing plugins no longer receive PermissionError for runtime class attribute writes.
  • Host event receiver fix: When the plugin host sent back grant_used or plugin_state, the receiver treated PluginManager as the outer application object and accessed plugin_manager on it, raising AttributeError. The manager now handles grant consumption and plugin-state refresh itself; host handshake, plugin state and one-time grant callbacks work again.

🆕 What's new in 4.0.14

  • Structured denials: Interceptions are still PermissionError and the message text is unchanged, but the exception now carries code, the permission bit, capability, target, layer, retryability, unlock entry and cooldown milliseconds, so plugins can branch on code instead of guessing from text.
  • Introspection and fallbacks: New api.can, api.explain, api.capabilities, api.permission_state, api.on_denial, api.call_with_fallback and api.declare_degraded; request_permission returns a bool-compatible PermissionResult that distinguishes undeclared, not granted, remembered deny, cooldown, rate limit, busy, timeout and cancel.
  • Four-layer attribution: Declaration L1, Grant L2, Scope L3 and Enforcement L4. The Security Center adds a Restriction layer column and the interception card names the layer, so "the permission is there but it still fails" points straight at the protected zone.
  • Four new permission bits: UI_READ (read UI structure), UI_MUTATE (rewrite widget classes, replacing the old reuse of UI_INJECT for class attribute writes), PLUGIN_CALL (call another plugin's services) and PLUGIN_DATA_SHARE (cross-plugin data).
  • Continue after approval: Once a prompt grants the permission, the intercepted operation continues immediately — no exception, no retry.
  • Observation mode: The reflection dunder guard, cross-plugin services and data sharing, and the api._app facade only record for now; security events are tagged observe with what would have been blocked.
  • Silent allowances fixed: API permission checks no longer treat failure as allow, suppressed-window checks leave a structured record, and service and content-provider registration join the permission surface.
  • Plugin compatibility: The manifest structure is unchanged and existing plugins keep working. To use the new capabilities, raise api_version to 3 and declare the new permissions in permissions_v2.on_demand.

🆕 What's new in 4.0.13

  • Automatic fade when the pointer is near: With click-through on, the window smoothly fades within 180 ms once the pointer enters a band about 38 px beyond its edge, down to roughly half of your configured opacity (never below 32%). Moving about 78 px away restores the original opacity. The enter and leave distances differ so the window does not flicker at the boundary.
  • Independent windows: Each floating window measures the pointer distance on its own, so one window fading does not affect the others. Only windows with click-through enabled take part, and turning click-through off or entering fullscreen restores the original opacity at once.
  • Configuration untouched: The fade is a temporary display effect; the saved opacity is never rewritten.
  • Plugin compatibility: This release does not change the plugin manifest structure.

🆕 What's new in 4.0.11

  • State-aware menu icons: Pin and unpin, click-through on and off, and window lock on and off now each use a different glyph — a pushpin when pinned and a struck-through pushpin when not, a slashed mouse when click-through is on and a plain mouse when off, a closed padlock when locked and an open padlock when unlocked. The icon updates as soon as the item is toggled.
  • Four menus unified: The countdown window, floating widget, pomodoro and plugin action menus now share one set of 16 px vector stroke icons with a 1.6 px stroke. Colour-mode entries, theme sub-items, zoom, remove-widget, start/pause, reset and skip entries that previously used an icon font are replaced as well, so two icon styles no longer mix.
  • Theme aware: Icon colours come from the theme tokens — body text colour when inactive, accent when checked, danger colour for destructive items — and stay legible in both light and dark themes.
  • Plugin compatibility: This release does not change the plugin manifest structure.

🆕 What's new in 4.0.12

  • Delete skins from the library: Custom skins can now be deleted from the action bar at the bottom of the skin library; the built-in Classic skin has no delete entry. If any projects use the skin, they are listed and deletion is confirmed twice, and those projects fall back to the default skin.
  • Plugin compatibility: This release does not change the plugin manifest structure, so plugin authors do not need to edit their manifests.

🆕 What's new in 4.0.10

  • Horizontal property tabs: The right panel now uses one row of Font, Colour, Background, General, Effects and Layout tabs. Clicking a tab switches the page and only one page is shown at a time; element-specific settings live in their matching tab instead of stacked collapsible groups.
  • Per-skin countdown format: Each skin now stores its own countdown display format and template, so editing or saving one skin no longer affects another. The Classic skin stays on decimal-days timing.
  • Custom format unit completion: When a template's {days} / {hours} / {minutes} / {seconds} placeholder lacks a unit, the renderer appends 天 / 时 / 分 / 秒 automatically; the insert buttons also add the unit text.
  • Plugin compatibility: This release does not change the plugin manifest structure, so plugin authors do not need to edit their manifests.

🆕 What's new in 4.0.9

  • In-place skin editing: Select a custom skin in the library and click Edit. The editor loads that skin's light/dark appearance, and saving overwrites the original instead of forcing a new one. Built-in skins remain read-only and can still be saved as a new skin.
  • Verse Flow auto contrast: Text colour is no longer hard-coded white. With Follow background enabled it switches according to the background behind it, using dark text on light and light text on dark, and recalculates when the window background changes. Picking a colour manually turns it off and fixes the colour.
  • Property categories: The top of the right panel is now split into collapsible Font, Colour, Background, General, Effects and Layout categories, with element-specific settings after them.
  • Background relocation: Element background is no longer a separate block at the bottom of the element properties. It joins window opacity, background type and window background colour/gradient/image/dynamic options under Background, and window background remains reachable with no element selected.

🆕 What's new in 4.0.8

  • Context menu icons: Settings, Always on top, Click through, Window lock, Fullscreen and Exam mode now use one 16 px stroke icon set with a uniform 1.6 px stroke; the icon-to-text gap drops from about 40 px to 9 px.
  • Checked and destructive items: Checked items use a neutral highlight, so Window lock no longer shows a red background. Close and Quit each get a separator and use the danger colour for icon and text.
  • Click-through icon: A slashed mouse replaces the pointer arrow.

🆕 What's new in 4.0.7

  • Bilingual help center: Titles and bodies for all 8 groups and 44 topics now live in data/help_zh.json and data/help_en.json. Switching the interface language also switches the help body, navigation tree, breadcrumb and group index. Missing English text falls back to the Chinese original with a notice.
  • Two-tier permission model: Baseline permissions are confirmed once when a plugin is enabled; on-demand permissions are requested only when the feature is actually used. Grant options are Allow once, This session, Always allow and Deny and remember. See [[ref:permission-model]].
  • Manifest v2: The new permissions_v2 block declares both tiers; the legacy integer permissions is migrated by risk.

🔁 Manifest changes for plugin authors

Replace the integer permission mask with permissions_v2: put low- and medium-risk permissions in baseline, and everything else in on_demand with a per-entry reason.

{
  "name": "stock-widget",
  "version": "1.0",
  "permissions_v2": {
    "baseline": ["FILE_READ", "NETWORK_HTTP", "THREAD_SPAWN"],
    "on_demand": [
      {"perm": "FILE_DELETE", "feature": "Cache cleanup", "title": "Delete cache files",
       "reason": "Remove temporary quote cache created by this plugin", "fallback": false},
      {"perm": "COMMAND", "feature": "Export report", "title": "Run local converter",
       "reason": "Invoke the bundled converter to export the report", "fallback": false}
    ]
  }
}
  • baseline accepts only permissions at or below medium risk and is capped at 12 entries; excess entries are truncated from highest risk down.
  • on_demand is capped at 24 entries; a missing reason makes the host show “The plugin did not explain what this is used for.”
  • fallback applies only to network access and clipboard. When set to true, a blocked operation triggers one prompt; after approval the operation continues automatically, with no plugin retry needed.
  • Keep the integer permissions only for compatibility with older hosts; this release uses permissions_v2.
